text:
maria: Quick QA — I noticed after the embed-service change that batches with empty string and null items sometimes produce fewer vectors than inputs. Downstream alignment relies on 1:1. Was the contract intentionally changed?

sam: We shouldn't change 1:1. The contract is: response.embeddings.length == inputs.length. If an item fails it should be `null` for that slot, not drop it. Can you paste an example request/response?

maria: repro below (made small):
```json
POST /v1/embeddings
{
  "model": "redwood-embed-sml-v2",
  "input": ["hello", "", null, "world"]
}
```
Observed response: we sometimes get 2 vectors instead of 4: 
```json
{
  "embeddings": [ [0.01, -0.2, ...], [0.12, 0.03, ...] ]
}
```
Which breaks the mapping.

kevin: Yikes. That's a regression. The spec in repo (api/embeddings.md) says preserve slots. If a backend skips empty or sentinel values during batching for performance we still need to rehydrate. Is that rehydration missing?

jules: I remember a perf change in the batching layer (PR #4321) that filters out empty strings before sending to model to avoid wasted tokens. We added a comment about rehydrate but maybe didn't wire it up for mixed nulls. I'll check the PR.

olga: Proposal: two behaviors depending on header: `X-Embeds-Strict: true` => respond with `null` placeholders and track original indexes; default (no header) => try to coalesce but still return same-length array (zero vector for empty?). Which do folks prefer? :thinking_face:

sam: I prefer preserving 1:1 by default. Returning `null` communicates failure; zero-vector is dangerous (silently changes semantics). So default should be `null` placeholders.

kevin: Agreed. Also add a compatibility note: if `input` contains explicit `null` values they should map to `null` in output without trying to call the model. Empty-string is trickier — we either call the model (and get a vector) or short-circuit to an explicit zero vector or `null`. Lean `null`.

jules: I can update PR #4321 to rehydrate and return `null` for both empty string and null inputs unless the user opts in with `X-Embeds-Empty-Policy: embed` to force embedding empty strings. That gives opt-in for folks relying on a vector for empty text.

maria: That sounds reasonable. Two asks: 1) Can we add an integration test that sends mixed inputs and asserts `embeddings.length == inputs.length` and correct null slots? 2) Update SDK doc blurb + our migration note.

olga: I'll add an ADR summarizing decision (null by default, opt-in header to embed empties) and list expected responses.

jules: PR pushed with fix + test. cc @kevin for review.

ci-bot: Build passed (linux, py39) — tests 142/142 ✅

kevin: Reviewing now, will add comments on naming and docs. One nit: name header `X-Embeds-Empty` with values `embed|null` to keep it short.

pr-bot: PR #4321 merged into main by jules — changelog entry added: "embeddings: rehydrate empty/null inputs; return null placeholders by default; opt-in header to embed empties". :tada:

maria: Awesome, thanks everyone. I'll coordinate SDK release notes in the docs channel and flag potential downstream consumers (vectorize-service) to check integration.

sam: FYI ops: we should monitor a spike in traffic if clients opt into embedding empties (more model calls). Add a dashboard alert on embed qps for a week.

olga: Noted — I'll create a brief runbook for handling regressions where rehydrate map fails (should be rare).

maria: Closing the loop: will follow up with a short message in #product and tag major customers that requested strict behavior. Thanks!
